rationale: P5 of the order intake (P4 plan §4; owner GO 2026-08-26, and the owner's explicit 2026-08-31 instruction 'please go ahead with the build release wiring'). The gap, in the plan's own words: seed_build_queue creates no site_specs aspects at all and upsertSite inserts only (domain, name, network_id, status) — so a customer's site arrives with NO register, hence no numeric-claim scan, and no contact details for the platform to verify a published address against. This is the stated reason seed 661 ships its collector DISABLED, and it is now the only thing between the first real PAID order (36744bf0, reference BR-9AUZ59, paid 2026-08-27 — verified at billing_orders AND the Stripe dashboard) and the first customer-shaped build. The change: a new seedCustomerIdentity helper called inside seed_build_queue's existing per-entry transaction, BEFORE insertWorkItem, so a build is armed before the first work item exists. It fires only when the direction jsonb carries the intake's customer fields (customer_email / customer_name — collect_external_orders is today's only writer of those keys at collect_external_orders_action.go:185-191, but any future producer threading the same keys gets the same arming without naming it); it writes sites.email and sites.company_name with existing-value-wins COALESCE (an operator's correction outranks the intake answer that predates it); and it seeds a minimal evidence_base register — two kind='entity' facts (business_name, contact) in the live register's exact fact shape (id/kind/claim/source.attested_by/verified_at, matched against webdesign.uk's own current register rather than guessed), marked as the CUSTOMER's attestations with the order reference in the attestation line. The no-clobber rule is a property of the SQL, not caller discipline: the INSERT carries WHERE NOT EXISTS (current evidence_base), so a re-seed after a lost ack cannot wipe a register somebody enriched. Three mutations were run and each killed its test: unconditional firing (the no-intake test's sqlmock fails on the unexpected UPDATE), COALESCE argument swap (pinned regex fails), and dropping the WHERE NOT EXISTS arm (pinned regex fails). Deliberately NOT done: no phone seeding (the direction payload does not carry one today); no writer_block/banned_claims invention (those are editorial constructs the platform derives; the seeded schema_notes says plainly the register is the customer's attestations and should be enriched, not assumed complete); no touching sites.name (upsertSite owns it); no enabling of the 661 task in this change (Go is inert until a roll — the seed's header now instructs verifying ancestry at the running stamp before flipping it on).

plan.summary: seed_build_queue gains seedCustomerIdentity: an intake-sourced build (direction carrying customer_email/customer_name, threaded by collect_external_orders) gets the customer's contact details written onto its sites row and a minimal two-fact evidence_base register seeded, inside the same transaction that files the first work item — arming the numeric/contact honesty guards BEFORE anything builds. Non-intake builds are untouched; existing site values and an existing register always win; three tests pin the behaviour and each named mutation kills one.

edits.rationale: The P5 arming itself, as a helper with the three load-bearing boundaries in one place: fires only on non-blank customer fields; existing-value-wins COALESCE on sites.email/company_name; the evidence_base INSERT guarded by WHERE NOT EXISTS so no-clobber is a property of the SQL, not caller discipline.

One call site, inside the existing per-entry transaction and BEFORE insertWorkItem, so 'armed before the first work item exists' is literal; a failure follows the action's existing per-entry idiom (rollback, skipped++, continue) and cannot poison other entries.

Three tests, each the kill-switch for a named mutation: arming happens with the pinned SQL and both facts + reference in the payload; non-intake directions (nil, objective-only, adopt_from, blank fields) touch the database not at all (sqlmock fails on any unexpected call); an existing register surviving (0 rows affected) is success, not error.

plan.risks: Blast radius is every seed_build_queue entry, so the reviewer should check the non-intake path stays byte-identical: the helper's only call is guarded by its own no-op arm (blank/absent customer fields return nil before any SQL), and the no-intake test enforces zero database calls for nil/objective/adopt_from shapes. The seeded register is deliberately minimal (two entity facts) — if a downstream reader assumes richer evidence_base keys (writer_block, banned_claims) it must already tolerate their absence, since refresh_evidence_base and hand-seeded registers vary; worth one reviewer glance at criteria_facts.go's reading arm. The sites UPDATE can touch a pre-existing site row for a re-collected domain, but only to fill EMPTY email/company_name (COALESCE existing-first, regex-pinned). Failure of either write rolls back the entry's whole transaction including the work item, leaving the build_queue row 'queued' for the next tick — the action's existing retry shape.
